content:
The image shows an orange (citrus fruit) with a distinctive fluffy, whisker-like white/blue-gray fungal growth covering the lower half of the fruit. The mycelium has long, hair-like filaments radiating outward — classic "whisker" morphology associated with *Rhizopus* or similar mold species. The upper portion of the fruit remains intact and orange-colored.

This is clearly **not** Huanglongbing (HLB/citrus greening), which affects leaves and causes yellow mottling, blotchy mottle patterns, and asymmetric leaf chlorosis — not fungal fruiting bodies on the fruit surface.

The fluffy, elongated hyphal strands (whiskers) on the fruit surface are the hallmark of **Whisker Mold**.
